$comment: The platforms this repository generates agent adapters for, and what each
one can actually enforce. Read by tools/agents/generate_adapters.py and
The roster is not listed here: it is whatever exists under .agents/agents/,
so adding an agent is adding one file. A manifest that also lists the
agents is a second place to forget.

how: A PreToolUse hook. `.claude/settings.json` runs
tools/agents/deny_writes_hook.py before every Write, Edit, MultiEdit or
NotebookEdit call. The hook input names the calling subagent in
`agent_type`, and a call from an agent whose canonical definition says
`writes: none` is refused.
Not the `tools:` frontmatter key, which is what this said until #326. A
probe had sacm-conformance-verifier (`tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash`) call
Write and Edit successfully: subagents run in the background by default,
and a background subagent is given Write and Edit whatever `tools:` lists.
`tools:` and `disallowedTools:` are still emitted, and nothing relies on them.
The hook covers those tools and nothing else. `Bash` is still granted,
because a read-only role has to be able to build and run things, and a shell
can write a file. The hook also holds only while project hooks run: a session
with hooks disabled, or a machine that cannot start Python, refuses nothing.
The generated paragraph states both remainders.
`sandbox_mode = "read-only"` in the agent file. Codex agent files accept
config.toml keys beyond the three required ones, and this is the one that
restricts writes; the documented example of a read-only explorer agent has
exactly this shape.
Unlike Claude's `tools:` list, the sandbox covers shell commands too, so
there is no instruction-only remainder to state here.
This was recorded as unenforceable when the package landed, on the strength
of the committed .toml files carrying only name, description and
developer_instructions. That was a fact about what had been written, not
about what the format supports.
